problems.title: Sofa angle monotonicity
problems.words: As a hallway's turn gets sharper, the best sofa should get smaller. Prove it between 60° and 90°.
problems.math: Let $A(\theta)$ be the maximal sofa area for a width-1 corridor turning by $\theta$. Prove $A$ is decreasing on $[\pi/3,\pi/2]$.

problems.title: Prime Nim, misère
problems.words: In Prime Nim where the last mover loses instead of wins, do the losing positions differ from normal play only finitely often?
problems.math: Compare the P-positions of the prime subtraction game in normal and misère play; decide whether their symmetric difference is finite.

problems.title: Counting 16 × 16 Sudoku
problems.words: Count the essentially different 16 × 16 Sudoku grids, ignoring symmetries, to three significant figures.
problems.math: Determine the automorphism group $\Gamma$ of the $16\times16$ Sudoku constraint structure and estimate $|\text{grids}/\Gamma|$ to 3 significant figures.

problems.title: Hyperbolic firefighter budgets
problems.words: In a hyperbolic tiling, fire spreads exponentially, so no fixed crew stops it. How fast must the crew grow?
problems.math: On the $\{7,3\}$ tiling graph, find the minimal growth of budgets $k_t$ (firefighters at turn $t$) that contains any single fire.

problems.title: Self-avoiding walks on the hat tiling
problems.words: Count paths across hat tiles that never revisit a tile, and show their growth rate is new.
problems.math: Prove the connective constant $\mu_{\text{hat}}$ exists for the hat adjacency graph and $\mu_{\text{hat}}\ne\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}$.

problems.title: S and Z Tetris
problems.words: If only the S and Z pieces ever come, how many lines can you clear before losing on a 10-wide board?
problems.math: On a $10\times20$ Tetris well with an adversarial sequence from $\{S,Z\}$, determine the maximum number of lines the player can guarantee.

problems.title: Square-sum spectral gap
problems.words: Find how well connected the square-sum graph is, through its eigenvalues.
problems.math: Determine the asymptotics of $\lambda_1(S_N)-\lambda_2(S_N)$ for the adjacency spectrum.

problems.title: Distant-force blow-up
problems.words: The 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up pushed fluid right where it broke. Make it break with a push kept far away.
problems.math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ with $\operatorname{supp} f\cap B(x_*,1)=\emptyset$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes from rest blows up at $x_*$ in finite time.

problems.title: Two-to-one Keller maps
problems.words: Known Jacobian counterexamples cover most points three or more times. Is there one covering most points exactly twice?
problems.math: Decide whether some $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ has generic fiber size exactly 2.

problems.title: Building a firebreak
problems.words: Firefighters must build one connected wall, one cell per turn, each next to the last. Can they ever enclose the fire?
problems.math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, each turn add one protected cell 8-adjacent to the previous one. Decide whether a single fire can be enclosed, and for which build rates.

problems.title: Benford orbits
problems.words: The leading digits of largest-factor Collatz orbits should follow Benford's law.
problems.math: Prove that for almost all $n$ the leading digits of $(f^k(n))_{k\le T(n)}$ satisfy Benford's law as $n\to\infty$.

problems.title: Kepler, compressed
problems.words: Make the computer-checked proof of the densest sphere packing far shorter.
problems.math: Give a Lean 4 proof of the Kepler conjecture in under 100,000 lines.

problems.title: Hat random walk diffusivity
problems.words: A random walk across hat tiles should look like ordinary Brownian motion from far away. Find its exact spreading rate.
problems.math: Prove the simple random walk on the hat adjacency graph satisfies an invariance principle with isotropic covariance $\sigma^2 I$, and compute $\sigma^2$.

problems.title: A four-dimensional einstein
problems.words: Find one 4D shape that fills 4D space but only without repeating.
problems.math: Find a connected tile $T\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ that tiles $\mathbb{R}^4$ by isometries but admits no periodic tiling.

problems.title: Random polykites
problems.words: Show almost no shapes made of many kites can tile the plane.
problems.math: Prove the fraction of $k$-kite polykites that tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ decays exponentially in $k$.

problems.title: Hat isoperimetry
problems.words: Among groups of n hat tiles, how short can the boundary be? Find the exact constant.
problems.math: For the hat adjacency graph, prove $\min_{|A|=n}|\partial A|\sim c\sqrt n$ and compute $c$.

problems.title: Spot fires
problems.words: Fires throw embers ahead at random. Find the exact spreading speed.
problems.math: For a growth model where each burning site ignites a site at i.i.d. heavy-tailed displacement at rate 1, compute the asymptotic speed or growth exponent explicitly.

problems.title: Prime Golomb rulers
problems.words: Find the shortest ruler with marks only at prime positions where all distances between marks are different.
problems.math: For each $n$, determine the minimal $L$ such that some set of $n$ primes in an interval of length $L$ has all pairwise differences distinct; find its asymptotics.

problems.title: Explicit Navier–Stokes blow-up
problems.words: Write down a forced Navier–Stokes blow-up as an explicit formula instead of a computer-assisted construction.
problems.math: Give closed-form smooth $u_0,f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for which the Navier–Stokes solution blows up in finite time.

problems.title: Spiral staircase
problems.words: What is the biggest convex box-like object that can be carried up a given spiral staircase?
problems.math: Maximize volume over convex bodies admissible in a helical tube of square cross-section $1$, radius $2$, pitch $3$.

problems.title: Forced SQG blow-up
problems.words: Copy the 2026 forced Navier–Stokes blow-up for the surface quasi-geostrophic equation.
problems.math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ such that forced SQG on $\mathbb{R}^2$ from rest blows up in finite time.

problems.title: Hat dominating sets
problems.words: Find the smallest fraction of hat tiles that touch every other tile.
problems.math: Compute the asymptotic domination density of the hat adjacency graph.

problems.title: Emirp sieve
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes have reversals with no small prime factors.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ have $\operatorname{rev}(p)$ with all prime factors $>p^{0.1}$.

problems.title: Hex on hat boards, large
problems.words: Solve Hex on hat-tiled boards of side 9.
problems.math: Determine the winner of Hex on the hat-tiled rhombus board of side 9, with an explicit strategy.

problems.title: Sofa stability
problems.words: Show that any sofa nearly as big as Gerver's must look nearly like Gerver's.
problems.math: Prove a quantitative stability bound: $A(S)\ge A_G-\varepsilon$ implies $d_H(S,G)\le C\varepsilon^{\alpha}$ up to rigid motion.

problems.title: Seven-free almost-Sophie-Germain
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes p avoid the digit 7 and have 2p + 1 with few prime factors.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p$ have $\Omega(2p+1)\le3$.

problems.title: Keller maps over finite fields
problems.words: Count the polynomial maps of three variables over a finite field with constant Jacobian that happen to be bijections.
problems.math: For $F\in\mathbb{F}_p[x,y,z]^3$ of degree $\le3$ with $\det DF\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times$, find the asymptotic proportion inducing bijections of $\mathbb{F}_p^3$ as $p\to\infty$.

problems.title: Hat drum's first mode
problems.words: Strike a hat-shaped drum. Show its lowest tone vibrates with a single peak.
problems.math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenfunction of the hat polygon has exactly one interior critical point.

problems.title: Internal DLA on hats
problems.words: Release walkers one at a time from a hat tile; each stops at the first unoccupied tile. Show the occupied cluster becomes a round disc.
problems.math: For internal DLA on the hat adjacency graph with $n$ particles, prove the cluster rescaled by $\sqrt n$ converges to a Euclidean disc (with tile centres as positions).

problems.title: Seven-free primes as an additive basis
problems.words: Show every large number is a sum of a bounded number of seven-free primes.
problems.math: Prove there is $k$ such that every sufficiently large integer of suitable parity is a sum of at most $k$ primes with no decimal digit 7, and give an explicit $k$.

problems.title: Seven-free primes with prime digit sum
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes have no digit 7 and a digit sum that is itself prime.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ free of the decimal digit 7 with $s_{10}(p)$ prime.

problems.title: Square-sum ordering with bounded displacement
problems.words: Order all positive integers so neighbours always sum to squares, and no number moves more than a fixed distance from its natural place.
problems.math: Decide whether there is a bijection $\pi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\pi(i)+\pi(i+1)$ always a square and $\sup_i|\pi(i)-i|/\sqrt i<\infty$.

problems.title: Finite simple groups in Lean
problems.words: Turn the classification of finite simple groups into one computer-checked proof.
problems.math: Formalize the classification of finite simple groups in Lean 4.

problems.title: Cube-sum paths
problems.words: Arrange 1 to N in a line so neighbours add to perfect cubes, for every large N.
problems.math: Prove $C_N$ has a Hamiltonian path for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: Reverse-square cycles
problems.words: Square and reverse the digits, repeatedly. Show there are infinitely many different loops.
problems.math: Prove $R(n)=\operatorname{rev}(n^2)$ has infinitely many distinct cycles.

problems.title: Convex sofa
problems.words: Find the best convex sofa.
problems.math: Maximize area over convex sets admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor.

problems.title: Unattained hyperbolic sofa
problems.words: In strongly curved hyperbolic space the best sofa might not exist. Show when the maximum is never reached.
problems.math: Find $\kappa_0$ such that for curvature $-\kappa<-\kappa_0$ the hyperbolic sofa supremum is not attained.

problems.title: Sofa in curved space with a corner
problems.words: On a cone-shaped surface the hallway corner is the cone point. Find the best sofa.
problems.math: For the width-1 corridor on a flat cone of angle $\alpha$ with the inner corner at the apex, find the optimal sofa area as a function of $\alpha$.

problems.title: Square-sum edge-Hamiltonian
problems.words: Show every edge of the square-sum graph lies on a loop through all of 1 to N, for large N.
problems.math: Prove that for all large $N$, every edge of $S_N$ lies on a Hamiltonian cycle of $S_N$.

problems.title: Prime-sum Hamiltonian count
problems.words: Count the ways to arrange 1 to 2n in a circle so neighbours sum to primes. Find the growth rate.
problems.math: Let $H_n$ count Hamiltonian cycles of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$. Prove $\log H_n=(1+o(1))\,c\,n\log n$ and find $c$.

problems.title: Hat tilings of convex regions
problems.words: Show no convex polygon can be tiled exactly by hats.
problems.math: Prove no convex polygon is a finite union of interior-disjoint congruent hats (reflections allowed), or exhibit one.

problems.title: Sidon sets of hat tiles
problems.words: Pick hat tiles so all pairwise displacement vectors are distinct. How many can fit in a region of n tiles?
problems.math: Determine the asymptotics of the maximum size of $A\subseteq B_L$ (hat-tiled $L$-ball, tile centres) with all differences $a-a'$, $a\ne a'$, distinct.

problems.title: Keller monodromy is everything
problems.words: Show every symmetric group appears as the hidden symmetry group of the fibres of some 3D Jacobian-conjecture counterexample.
problems.math: Prove that for each $n\ge3$ there is a non-invertible Keller map $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ of geometric degree $n$ whose generic monodromy group is $S_n$.

problems.title: Real-rank hyperoperation uniqueness
problems.words: Prove there is exactly one natural way to fill in the operations between addition, multiplication and powers.
problems.math: Prove uniqueness of an analytic family $a[s]b$ on $s\in[1,3]$ under the recursion law plus a log-convexity condition in $s$, and existence.

problems.title: Squared squares with consecutive primes
problems.words: Find a perfect squared square whose square sides are consecutive primes.
problems.math: Find or rule out a perfect squared square whose component sides are $p_k,p_{k+1},\dots,p_{k+r}$ for some $k,r$.

problems.title: LF-Collatz stopping time distribution
problems.words: Find the exact distribution of how long the largest-factor Collatz map takes to settle.
problems.math: Prove $T_f(n)/\log n$ converges in distribution on $[1,x]$ and identify the limit law.

problems.title: 7×7 Othello
problems.words: Who wins Othello on an odd 7×7 board with a fixed off-centre start?
problems.math: Strongly solve Othello on a $7\times7$ board from the standard initial cross shifted to the corner-adjacent center.

problems.title: Firefighter on Z³
problems.words: How many firefighters per turn are needed to contain a fire in 3D, as a precise growth rate?
problems.math: Determine $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)/t$ for the minimal firefighters needed to contain fire on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ by time $t$.

problems.title: Origami with a bounded number of layers
problems.words: Find the best origami base for any tree when no point may have more than 4 layers of paper.
problems.math: Give an algorithm for the minimal square paper for uniaxial bases of metric trees with layer count at most 4, with proof of optimality.

problems.title: Beat the prism
problems.words: Gerver's sofa, lifted to one unit tall, can turn a corner in a square pipe. Find a 3D shape with more volume that can still make the turn.
problems.math: In the corridor $([0,1]\times\mathbb{R}\cup\mathbb{R}\times[0,1])\times[0,1]$ turning about the $z$-axis, find a rigid motion-admissible solid of volume $>2.2195\ldots$.

problems.title: Hardest Rush Hour
problems.words: Find the 7 × 7 Rush Hour traffic-jam puzzle that takes the most moves to solve.
problems.math: Over all solvable $7\times7$ Rush Hour configurations, determine $\max$ of the minimum solution length, with a certificate.

problems.title: Lean golf is NP-hard
problems.words: Show that finding the shortest proof using only a few basic Lean tactics is computationally hard.
problems.math: Prove NP-hardness of: given a Lean 4 goal and $k$ in unary, is there a proof using only intro, apply, exact, rfl with at most $k$ steps?

problems.title: Obtuse sofa
problems.words: The corridor turns 120° instead of 90°. Find a sofa and a matching upper bound within 1%.
problems.math: For a width-1 corridor with turn angle $2\pi/3$, find $A$ with an admissible sofa of area $A$ and a proof that the optimum is $<1.01A$.

problems.title: Fire on a cylinder
problems.words: A fire burns on a grid wrapped into an infinite tube of width n. How many firefighters per turn stop it?
problems.math: On $C_n\times\mathbb{Z}$ with 4-neighbour spread, find the least $k(n)$ that always contains a single fire, for every $n$.

problems.title: Adversarial 2048
problems.words: An opponent places every new tile in 2048 as unhelpfully as possible. What is the biggest tile you can still guarantee?
problems.math: On the $4\times4$ board where an adversary chooses each spawn's position and value in $\{2,4\}$, determine the largest tile the player can force.

problems.title: Seven-free Egyptian fractions
problems.words: Write every fraction as a sum of distinct unit fractions whose denominators never contain the digit 7.
problems.math: Prove every $q\in\mathbb{Q}\cap(0,1)$ is $\sum_{d\in D}1/d$ for a finite set $D$ of distinct integers with no decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Fewest KenKen cages
problems.words: What is the fewest cages for a uniquely solvable 6 × 6 KenKen puzzle?
problems.math: Minimize the number of cages in a $6\times6$ KenKen (cage targets with $+,-,\times,\div$) having a unique Latin-square solution.

problems.title: Integer sofa
problems.words: With the hallway scaled to width 10, what is the biggest polygon with whole-number corners that turns the corner?
problems.math: Maximize area over lattice polygons admissible in the width-10 right-angled corridor.

problems.title: Seven-free three primes
problems.words: Every large odd number should be a sum of three primes that never use the digit 7.
problems.math: Prove every sufficiently large odd $N$ is $p_1+p_2+p_3$ with each $p_i$ prime and free of the decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Two fires
problems.words: Two fires start a distance d apart. How many firefighters per turn are needed, depending on d?
problems.math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with 4-neighbour spread, find the least $k(d)$ containing fires started at $(0,0)$ and $(d,0)$.

problems.title: Hex on hats
problems.words: Play Hex on a board made of hat tiles. Can games end in a draw, and who wins on a small board?
problems.math: For Hex on hat-tiled rhombus boards, decide whether draws are possible, and solve side length 5.

problems.title: Worst-case Battleship
problems.words: What is the fewest shots that always sinks the standard fleet on a 10 × 10 board?
problems.math: Compute the minimax number of shots to sink ships of lengths 5,4,3,3,2 on $10\times10$ against an adversary who may move ships consistently with past answers.

problems.title: Sudoku resolution bounds
problems.words: Proving a large broken Sudoku has no solution should require long logical proofs.
problems.math: Prove resolution refutations of unsatisfiable $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku instances require size $2^{n^{\Omega(1)}}$ for some explicit family.

problems.title: Shuffle-sorting
problems.words: Using any of the six 3-pile perfect shuffles each time, how many shuffles reach any reachable arrangement in the worst case?
problems.math: Determine the diameter of the Cayley graph of the 3-pile shuffle group on $3n$ cards, asymptotically in $n$.

problems.title: The sofa's boundary is not algebraic
problems.words: Gerver's sofa is bounded by 18 curve pieces. Show some of them are not polynomial curves.
problems.math: Prove at least one boundary arc of Gerver's sofa is not contained in any algebraic curve.

problems.title: Random Wang tiles
problems.words: Pick n random tile types with colored edges. How likely are they to tile the plane?
problems.math: For $n$ Wang tiles with edge colours i.i.d. uniform in $[c]$, find the asymptotics of $\Pr(\text{tiles }\mathbb{Z}^2)$ as $n\to\infty$.

problems.title: Delayed fire on hexagons
problems.words: On a honeycomb grid, firefighters arrive one turn late. Find how many per turn are needed.
problems.math: On the hexagonal lattice with 3-neighbour spread and one-turn protection delay, find the least per-turn budget containing a single fire.

problems.title: Random-turn Prime Nim
problems.words: In Prime Nim where a coin flip decides who moves, find the exact winning chance from a pile of n.
problems.math: For random-turn play of the prime subtraction game, compute $\lim_n$ of the value from pile $n$, if it exists.

problems.title: Kissing spectres
problems.words: How many spectre tiles can touch one spectre without overlapping?
problems.math: Determine the maximal number of interior-disjoint congruent spectres meeting a fixed one.

problems.title: Hat Ising bounds
problems.words: Pin down the critical temperature of magnets on a hat tiling to within one percent.
problems.math: Prove two-sided bounds on $T_c$ for the hat-graph Ising model with ratio $\le1.01$.

problems.title: Sudoku symmetry breaking
problems.words: Show that most big Sudoku grids have no symmetry at all.
problems.math: Prove the proportion of $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku grids with nontrivial automorphism tends to 0.

problems.title: Twin hats
problems.words: Find a pair of different tiles that can each tile the plane only together, aperiodically, with a matching rule nobody has found yet.
problems.math: Find two polykites $A,B$ with $\le 6$ kites each, neither tiling alone, that together tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ only aperiodically.

problems.title: Cube-sum connectivity
problems.words: Join numbers that add to a perfect cube. Show everything links up once N is large.
problems.math: Prove $C_N$ ($a\sim b\iff a+b$ is a cube) is connected for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: Toroidal Othello
problems.words: Who wins Othello on an 8 × 8 board that wraps around?
problems.math: Weakly solve Othello on $\mathbb{Z}_8^2$ with standard initial position.

problems.title: Shrink to fit
problems.words: Find the largest size such that every convex shape no wider than that, measured end to end, gets around the corner.
problems.math: Find the largest $d$ such that every planar convex body of diameter $\le d$ is admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor.

problems.title: Prime and square neighbours
problems.words: Order all positive integers so neighbours add to a prime and numbers two apart add to a square.
problems.math: Decide whether there is a bijection $\pi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\pi_i+\pi_{i+1}$ prime and $\pi_i+\pi_{i+2}$ square for all $i$.

problems.title: Prime-graceful forests
problems.words: Label any forest so the edge differences are exactly the first m primes.
problems.math: Prove every forest with $m$ edges has an injective $\ell:V\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ whose edge differences are $\{p_1,\dots,p_m\}$.

problems.title: Tetris on a cylinder
problems.words: When the board wraps left to right, can a player survive forever against any piece sequence?
problems.math: Decide whether a player can survive indefinitely in a width-10 cylindrical Tetris well against adversarial piece sequences with 1-piece preview.

problems.title: Squared rectangles with prime sides
problems.words: Find the smallest perfect squared rectangle whose squares all have prime side lengths.
problems.math: Determine the minimal order of a perfect squared rectangle with every component side prime.

problems.title: Hat aperiodicity in Lean, minimal
problems.words: Give a computer-checked proof that the hat tiles only aperiodically, in under 2000 lines.
problems.math: Produce a Lean 4 proof of the hat's aperiodicity of at most 2000 lines using only Mathlib.

problems.title: Spectre chromatic number of distances
problems.words: Colour points of the plane so no two points at a distance equal to a spectre edge length or diagonal share a colour. Find the colours needed.
problems.math: Let $D$ be the set of distances between vertices of the spectre polygon. Determine $\chi(\mathbb{R}^2;D)$.

problems.title: Node Kayles on square sums
problems.words: Players alternately pick an unused number up to N that does not sum to a square with any picked number. Last to move wins. Decide the winner for large N.
problems.math: Determine the outcome of Node Kayles on $S_N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: The 7p+4 funnel, almost always
problems.words: Show almost every prime eventually falls into the 12-cycle of the 7p + 4 map.
problems.math: Prove the primes whose $p\mapsto P(7p+4)$ orbit enters its 12-cycle have relative density 1.

problems.title: Codes avoiding square distances
problems.words: Find the largest set of binary strings of length n in which no two differ in a perfect-square number of positions. Find the exponential rate.
problems.math: Let $A(n)$ be the largest $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ with $d_H(x,y)$ never a positive perfect square for $x\ne y\in C$. Determine $\lim_n\frac1n\log_2A(n)$.

problems.title: Seven-free primes with a large shifted factor
problems.words: Show a positive fraction of seven-free primes p have p − 1 with a prime factor bigger than p^0.6.
problems.math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: p\ \text{7-free},\ P(p-1)>p^{0.6}\}\gg\pi_7(x)$.

problems.title: Homogenized wildfire
problems.words: Fire spreads through random patches of two fuel types. Show it has a definite average speed and compute it.
problems.math: For the eikonal equation with i.i.d. two-valued speed on a lattice, prove homogenization and give the effective speed in closed form.

problems.title: Prime-indexed seven-free primes
problems.words: List the primes in order. Show infinitely many seven-free primes sit at a prime position in that list.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $p_q$ with $q$ prime and $p_q$ free of the decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Antiferromagnetic hats
problems.words: Colour hat tiles up or down to minimise same-colour neighbours. The hat graph has odd cycles, so some frustration is unavoidable. Compute the ground-state entropy exactly.
problems.math: For the antiferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph, prove the zero-temperature entropy per tile exists, is positive, and compute it in closed form.

problems.title: Square Nim from both ends
problems.words: Two piles; a move removes a square from one pile or the same square from both. Find the losing positions' asymptotic density.
problems.math: For moves $(a,b)\to(a-k^2,b),(a,b-k^2),(a-k^2,b-k^2)$, prove $\#\{(a,b)\in[N]^2:\mathcal P\}=N^{1+\theta+o(1)}$ and find $\theta$.

problems.title: Hat quasicrystal Ising universality, bond-disordered
problems.words: Randomly weaken some bonds in the hat Ising model. Show the critical behaviour still matches the clean 2D Ising class up to logs.
problems.math: For the random-bond ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph with i.i.d. couplings in $[1,1+\varepsilon]$, prove the specific heat diverges at most as $\log\log|t|^{-1}$ near $T_c$ for small $\varepsilon$.

problems.title: The last even loss in Prime Nim
problems.words: In Prime Nim almost every losing pile size is odd. The only even ones found are 0, 10, 34, 100 and 310. Prove there are no more.
problems.math: For the subtraction game with prime moves, prove $\{n \text{ even}: G(n)=0\}=\{0,10,34,100,310\}$.

problems.title: Few loops for square-plus-one
problems.words: The square-plus-one map has a loop: 89 goes to 233 and back. Show there are only finitely many loops.
problems.math: Prove $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$ has finitely many periodic orbits (one is $89\leftrightarrow233$).

problems.title: Hat Laplacian eigenvalue is transcendental
problems.words: Show the lowest vibration frequency of a hat-shaped drum with clamped edges is transcendental.
problems.math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ of the hat polygon (unit kite side) is transcendental.

problems.title: Undecidable prime-factor maps
problems.words: Show no algorithm can decide, given a and b, whether every orbit of n ↦ n/2 (even) or the largest prime factor of an + b (odd) eventually loops.
problems.math: Prove $\{(a,b)\in\mathbb{N}^2:$ every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ ($n$ even), $P(an+b)$ ($n$ odd) is eventually periodic$\}$ is not recursive, or prove it is.

problems.title: Square-plus-one orbits rarely loop
problems.words: Show almost every starting number's square-plus-one sequence never repeats.
problems.math: Prove the set of $n$ whose orbit under $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$ is eventually periodic has natural density 0.

problems.title: Square-plus-one orbit mod 3
problems.words: Show the square-plus-one sequence starting at 2 lands on primes of both kinds mod 3 infinitely often.
problems.math: Prove $Q^k(2)\equiv1\pmod 3$ and $Q^k(2)\equiv2\pmod 3$ each hold for infinitely many $k$.

problems.title: Hat packing density is irrational
problems.words: The densest packing of hats without reflections leaves gaps. Show the best density is an irrational number.
problems.math: Prove the maximal packing density of congruent hats under orientation-preserving isometries is irrational.

problems.title: Is eventual periodicity of square-plus-one decidable?
problems.words: Is there an algorithm that decides, for any n, whether its square-plus-one sequence eventually loops?
problems.math: Decide whether $\{n: (Q^k(n))_k \text{ is eventually periodic}\}$ is recursive, where $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$.

problems.title: Conformal radius of Gerver's sofa
problems.words: Map a disc conformally onto Gerver's sofa, sending the centre to the sofa's centroid. Show the scale factor is transcendental.
problems.math: Prove the conformal radius of Gerver's sofa at its centroid is transcendental.

problems.title: Gerver's constant is not a period
problems.words: Show the area of Gerver's sofa cannot be written as an integral of an algebraic function over an algebraic region.
problems.math: Prove $\mu_G\approx2.2195$ is not a Kontsevich–Zagier period.
